blocked.what: of all shot attempts, this many were blocked by a body (n counts ATTEMPTS, not games)

neverReachedTheGoalie.what: of all shot attempts, this many never reached the goalie — blocked or missed (n counts ATTEMPTS, not games)

reachedTheGoalie.what: of all shot attempts, this many reached the goalie (n counts ATTEMPTS, not games)

saveFraction.what: of the shots a goalie actually faced, this many were saved — an empty-net goal is not among them, and neither is a shootout attempt (n counts SHOTS FACED, not games, and is NOT goals + shots on goal)

moreAttemptsLost.what: the team with more shot attempts lost

moreLevelControlLost.what: the team that controlled play while the score was level lost

moreShotsOnGoalLost.what: the team with more shots on goal lost

drawStrength.what: face-offs split by whether the team that won them was at even strength or on the power play, and the shot attempts that team took before the next whistle set against the attempts the team that lost the draw took (n counts FACE-OFFS, not games). A draw won on the power play is followed by a power play, so this says what winning one is worth in that situation and not what the draw itself contributed.

endZone.what: shot attempts taken before the next whistle after an end-zone face-off, counted for the team attacking that end and for the team defending it, out of every end-zone face-off (n counts FACE-OFFS, not games). The defending team’s attempts are shots at the FAR end — what getting the puck out and back up the ice looks like — so the pair says how strongly play tends to stay where the whistle put it, and says nothing about the contest at the line itself, which leaves no event in the record.

faceoffZone.what: face-offs sorted by the zone the team that WON them was attacking toward, and the shot attempts each team took before the next whistle (n counts FACE-OFFS, not games). The offensive and defensive rows are the same draws seen from the two sides, so this cannot separate where a draw happened from who won it — endZone is the pair that can, because it splits by which team was attacking that end rather than by the winner.

hits.what: whether a team that lands more hits in a game also takes fewer shot attempts in it, measured two ways over every game we hold (n counts GAMES). The first is how strongly the two move together, where a negative number means they run opposite; the second asks the same thing without any assumption about the shape of the data — the share of games in which the team with more hits had fewer attempts. Hits are counted by each home rink’s own crew, and the same teams are credited with more of them at home than away, so this measures the scorers as well as the play.

pace.what: shot attempts taken in one situation, out of the minutes played in that situation, scaled to sixty — so a power-play rate and an even-strength rate can be set beside each other (attempts counts ATTEMPTS and minutes counts MINUTES, neither counts games). The power play and the penalty kill are divided by the SAME minutes, counted once from each side, as are trailing and leading.

shift.what: how long a skater’s shift lasts, in seconds, taken from the whole archive’s shifts rather than by averaging each game’s own middle value (n counts SHIFTS, not games). The middle half is the twenty-fifth to the seventy-fifth of them, which is a definition and not a band anybody chose. Goaltenders are left out, since a goaltender’s shift is most of the game, and a shift the record gives no end for is left out rather than counted as nothing.

shooter.what: shot attempts split by the position the roster lists for the player who took them, and for each group what became of those attempts — blocked, on goal, missed, or a goal (n counts ATTEMPTS, not games). Position is what the roster says and not a judgement about where a player was standing, so a defenceman who has walked to the top of the circle is still counted as one.

state.what: the minutes played in each situation and the goals scored in them, scaled to sixty — even strength, on the power play, and with a net empty (minutes counts MINUTES and goals counts GOALS, neither counts games). The unknown row is play whose skater count the record does not settle, and it is published even at zero because a bucket that appears only when it is full is one nobody notices arriving.

whistles.what: how often play stops for each reason across the archive, as counts rather than as rates: penalties called, plays ruled offside, pucks iced, power plays begun, and the goals scored by each side during them. A power play is counted where the advantage CHANGES, so it is not the same thing as a penalty — one trip to the box can be two of them, and one ends early when a goal is scored.

allowed.what: goals one goaltender allowed in one game (n counts GOALTENDER APPEARANCES, not games, and excludes the shootout)

faced.what: shots one goaltender faced in one game (n counts GOALTENDER APPEARANCES, not games, and excludes the shootout)

blocked.what: attempts a body stopped, both teams, in one game (n counts GAMES, not events)

corsi.what: shot attempts by both teams in one game, at all strengths (n counts GAMES, not events)

goaltending.what: shots the two goaltenders faced between them in one game (n counts GAMES, not events)

slot.what: shot attempts from inside the slot, both teams, in one game (n counts GAMES, not events)

whistle.what: whistles that stopped play in one game (n counts GAMES, not events)

zonestart.what: face-offs in one game, both teams, at all strengths (n counts GAMES, not events)

blocked.what: attempts a body stopped, both teams, in one game (n counts GAMES, not events)

blocked-shot.what: feet from the attacking net at which a blocked shot is RECORDED (n counts EVENTS, not games; for a blocked shot this is where the puck was stopped, which is the BLOCKER's position and not where the shot was taken)

goal.what: feet from the attacking net at which a goal is RECORDED (n counts EVENTS, not games; for a blocked shot this is where the puck was stopped, which is the BLOCKER's position and not where the shot was taken)

missed-shot.what: feet from the attacking net at which a missed shot is RECORDED (n counts EVENTS, not games; for a blocked shot this is where the puck was stopped, which is the BLOCKER's position and not where the shot was taken)

shot-on-goal.what: feet from the attacking net at which a shot on goal is RECORDED (n counts EVENTS, not games; for a blocked shot this is where the puck was stopped, which is the BLOCKER's position and not where the shot was taken)

rule: even-strength shot attempts taken while the score was level, in regulation

attempts.what: of the unblocked shot attempts whose location the feed records, this many were taken from inside the slot — within 33 ft of the attacking net and inside 22 ft of centre (n counts ATTEMPTS, not games, and a blocked shot is excluded because the coordinate the feed records for one is the BLOCKER's, not the shooter's)

scoredFromInside.what: of the unblocked attempts taken from INSIDE the slot, this many were goals (n counts ATTEMPTS, not games, over the games carrying BOTH goal and attempt placement)

scoredFromOutside.what: of the unblocked attempts taken from OUTSIDE the slot, this many were goals (n counts ATTEMPTS, not games, over the games carrying BOTH goal and attempt placement)

slot.what: of the goals scored in play whose location the feed records, this many were taken from inside the slot — within 33 ft of the attacking net and inside 22 ft of centre (n counts GOALS, not games, and excludes the shootout)
